children: Bank of Queensland's bear at Macquarie reckons the Australian lender is still in a tough position despite its recent margin expansion. Analyst Jason Shao points out that BOQ's better-than-expected second-half net interest margin was supported by a deliberate reduction in the size of its balance sheet. He warns clients in a note that scale is needed to improve overall returns, but expects margin pressures to re-emerge as BOQ starts growing its mortgage book again. He struggles to see how BOQ can improve return-on-tangible equity beyond 8%. Macquarie keeps an underperform rating on the stock with a target price of 5.50 Australian dollars. Shares are down 0.15% at A$6.86. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
